title: Prompt Engineering vs. Evaluation Engineering: Know the Difference
author: Jason D.
excerpt: Prompt engineering gets you demos. Evaluation engineering gets you production. Here's why the shift matters and how to make it.
content:
Prompt engineering has become the default starting point for most AI projects. Tweak the prompt, test a few examples, ship it. It works for demos. It fails in production.

The Difference

Prompt engineering is about crafting the right instructions for the model. It's important, but it's one piece of the system.

Evaluation engineering is about building the infrastructure to measure whether the entire system — prompts, models, data pipelines, and business rules — is working correctly.

# Prompt engineering gives you:
- A good demo
- Anecdotal evidence
- "It works on these 5 examples"

# Evaluation engineering gives you:
- Automated testing on 500+ scenarios
- Regression detection
- Performance trending over time
- Confidence in production readiness

Why the Shift Matters

Prompt engineering is necessary but not sufficient. Here's why:

  • Prompts are fragile — small changes can have large, unexpected effects
  • You can't manually test every scenario
  • Production data is messier than test data
  • Models get updated, and behavior changes
  • Edge cases only surface at scale

Making the Shift

You don't have to abandon prompt engineering. Just wrap it in evaluation:

  • Every prompt change triggers the eval suite
  • Every new edge case gets added to the test set
  • Every deployment has a quality gate based on eval results
  • Every week includes a review of eval trends

Prompt engineering without evaluation is art. Evaluation engineering is science. Production systems need both, but they need the science more.

The Bottom Line

If you're spending 80% of your time on prompts and 20% on evaluation, flip it. Build the evaluation framework first. Then optimize prompts with confidence, because you'll actually know whether your changes helped or hurt.
